input.question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?
input.ground_truth: Most indoor malls depend on the very large "anchor" stores to pull people in. These are your Macy's, Nordstrom, and other department stores, for the most part. These stores aren't doing nearly as well with the advent of online shopping, so the foot traffic to the other stores suffer. With less foot traffic, the smaller stores start to shutter, and it becomes a cycle. Strip malls are significantly less expensive and don't depend on their anchor stores in the same way.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why are indoor-only shopping malls dying in the USA?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big toy box at home where you can play with all your toys. But then, your parents say you can now go outside and play with your friends at the park, where you can also see butterflies, trees, and even visit other kids’ houses.

Now, think of the shopping mall as that toy box. A long time ago, people had to go to the mall to buy toys, clothes, and see their friends. But now, people can buy almost anything they want on the computer or their phone, right from home! Also, they can go to big stores outside, like big playgrounds with lots of things to see and do, not just shopping.

So, fewer people are going to the indoor-only malls because they can do the same things (or even better things) outside, on the internet, or in bigger, more fun places. That’s why those old malls are having a hard time.
